The Child Who Tries to Eat Before the Grown-Ups

At a meal with the whole family gathered, before the grown-ups have even sat down, a hungry child reaches out their chopsticks first. Scolding makes the mood awkward, but letting it slide leaves you worried about manners.

A child trying to eat first isn't being rude—they're simply hungry and not yet used to waiting. What's needed here isn't a scolding, but warm guidance that helps them feel how much nicer it is to eat together.

Curious about the story of children's table manners? Let's look at the lesson through the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the story too. Read "children's table manners" with your little one and talk about it together. We've gathered all kinds of stories about "14. Everyone Sit Down and Enjoy!"—table etiquette, table manners stories, consideration stories, and more.
content.caption: Trying to eat first isn't a matter of being rude.

content.text:
Why Eating Together with Manners Matters

Table manners aren't just rules—they're a process of learning to consider others and know how to wait. In the time spent waiting for the grown-ups and greeting one another as they eat together, a child naturally builds a sense of consideration and community.

What matters is not forcing manners, but building up the experience that eating together is tastier and more joyful. The warmth of a meal where everyone shares side dishes and talks together teaches a child the reason behind manners.
content.caption: Learn why food tastes better when you eat together.

content.alt: 14. Everyone Sit Down and Enjoy! - Toto's Everyone-Sit-Down Story
content.text:
Toto's Everyone-Sit-Down Story

In "Everyone Sit Down and Enjoy!" Toto is so hungry that he reaches out his chopsticks to eat before Grandpa. When Hoya asks, "Huh? What about Grandpa?" he finally notices the empty seat of honor.

Grandpa comes in chuckling and takes his hand, saying, "Food tastes better when we all sit down together." Hori teaches the rule—"When the grown-ups pick up their spoons first, then we all say, 'Thank you for the food!'"—and when the whole family eats together, the meal really is more delicious. Sharing side dishes, the laughter never stops.
content.caption: Grandpa's words: food tastes better when we all sit down.

content.alt: 14. Everyone Sit Down and Enjoy! - Let's Practice Together at Home
content.text:
Let's Practice Together at Home

After reading, connect the story to your own family's meals. First, rather than forcing manners as mere rules, help them feel that eating together is tastier.

Second, decide on your family's own table rules together with your child, like "after the grown-ups pick up their spoons first" and "let's all say, thank you for the food." Third, make frequent time for the whole family to sit down together, and share side dishes while you talk. A shared meal is the best manners education there is.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q. At what age should I start teaching children's table manners?

A. From the time they start holding a spoon on their own, you can gradually teach them by sitting down and enjoying meals together. What matters is letting them experience a joyful table before perfection.

Q. Why is the habit of eating all together important?

A. When the family sits down to eat together, a child naturally learns the joy of a meal and its manners. Time spent sitting down and enjoying a meal all together is the best classroom for children's table manners.

Q. How do I teach table manners in a fun way?

A. Share greetings like "thank you for the meal" and the joy of eating together as if it were play. When you praise them warmly for keeping the manners, a child comes to want to keep them on their own.
